title: Tiered Add-ons Pilot: Observability Retention, Compliance Bundle, and Premium SLA Packaging
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary: Run a tiered add-ons pilot targeting enterprise signups to validate willingness-to-pay and operational costs for three bundled features: (1) Observability retention tiers (7/30/90 days), (2) Compliance bundle (SOC2 scope, audit logs, customer-managed KMS, VPC peering support), and (3) Premium SLA (99.95% uptime, 24/7 on-call, priority incident response).

Hypothesis: Packaging these features into discrete, priced add-ons (monthly subscription + per-token discount) will increase net new ARR and reduce churn on high-usage customers, while preserving our unit economics if storage and SRE costs are controlled.

Experiment design: A three-arm cohort experiment for qualifying enterprise leads and self-serve upgraded accounts: control (no add-ons), bundle A (Observability + SLA), bundle B (Compliance + SLA). Pricing bands proposed: Starter Add-ons ($500/mo base, + per-token pricing unchanged), Premium Add-ons ($2,000/mo base with 10% per-token discount), Enterprise Add-ons (custom pricing + negotiated contract). Run window: 90 days with interim checkpoints at 30/60 days. Success metrics: conversion rate to paid add-on, ARR uplift per cohort, MRR churn delta vs baseline, gross margin impact, and NPS change for customers on add-ons.

Operational requirements & gating: Engineering changes needed for retention (tiered cold storage + index for queries) tracked in ENG-2841. Feature flags per-org to gate retention and compliance features. Contract/legal changes: updated security questionnaire responses, new contract exhibit for compliance controls, and SLA language for credits — Legal review required (see attachments). Billing: Console UI changes for enabling/disabling add-ons + line-item billing; Billing flow tracked with FIN-ops for invoice templates.

Trade-offs considered:
- Longer retention increases storage costs and possible egress charges; mitigation: compressed storage + delayed hot-path retrieval with explicit pricing.
- Compliance features add one-time engineering delta for integrations (KMS, VPC) and recurring validation cost; propose charging a one-time onboarding fee for Enterprise tier.
- SLA increases operational burden; we recommend a tiered on-call rotation with paged coverage for Enterprise SLA and a higher MRR threshold before SLA activation.

Contract/security questionnaire implications: We must update our standard questionnaire answers for customers who purchase the Compliance bundle (SOC2 scope, encryption at rest keys: customer-managed KMS, and audit log retention policies). Legal requests updated sample clauses for inclusion in the master services agreement (MSA) and a checklist for SOC2 evidence collection.

Rollout plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha): offer to 5 existing enterprise customers for feedback (Mar 2025). Phase 1 (pilot): open to new enterprise signups with Sales enablement + playbook (Apr–Jun 2025). Phase 2 (general availability): console self-serve and Marketplace listing (H2-2025) if metrics meet thresholds.

Artifacts: PRD, pricing model spreadsheet, sample SLA language, and experiment dashboard links below.
